verses.text: But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
Early in the morning He went back into the temple courts. All the people came to Him, and He sat down to teach them.
The scribes and Pharisees, however, brought to Him a woman caught in adultery. They made her stand before them
and said, "Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery.
In the Law Moses commanded us to stone such a woman. So what do You say?"
They said this to test Him, in order to have a basis for accusing Him. But Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with His finger.
When they continued to question Him, He straightened up and said to them, "Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her."
And again He bent down and wrote on the ground.
When they heard this, they began to go away one by one, beginning with the older ones, until only Jesus was left, with the woman standing there.
Then Jesus straightened up and asked her, "Woman, where are your accusers? Has no one condemned you?"
"No one, Lord," she answered. "Then neither do I condemn you," Jesus declared. "Now go and sin no more."
Once again, Jesus spoke to the people and said, "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life."
So the Pharisees said to Him, "You are testifying about Yourself; Your testimony is not valid."
Jesus replied, "Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I came from or where I am going.
You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.
But even if I do judge, My judgment is true, because I am not alone; I am with the Father who sent Me.
Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid.
I am One who testifies about Myself, and the Father, who sent Me, also testifies about Me."
"Where is Your Father?" they asked Him. "You do not know Me or My Father," Jesus answered. "If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well."
He spoke these words while teaching in the temple courts, near the treasury. Yet no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.
Again He said to them, "I am going away, and you will look for Me, but you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come."
So the Jews began to ask, "Will He kill Himself, since He says, 'Where I am going, you cannot come'?"
Then He told them, "You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world.
That is why I told you that you would die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins."
"Who are You?" they asked. "Just what I have been telling you from the beginning," Jesus replied.
"I have much to say about you and much to judge. But the One who sent Me is truthful, and what I have heard from Him, I tell the world."
They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.
So Jesus said, "When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He, and that I do nothing on My own, but speak exactly what the Father has taught Me.
He who sent Me is with Me. He has not left Me alone, because I always do what pleases Him."
As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.
So He said to the Jews who had believed Him, "If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples.
Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free."
"We are Abraham's descendants," they answered. "We have never been slaves to anyone. How can You say we will be set free?"
Jesus replied, "Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who sins is a slave to sin.
A slave does not remain in the house forever, but a son remains forever.
So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
I know you are Abraham's descendants, but you are trying to kill Me because My word has no place within you.
I speak of what I have seen in the presence of the Father, and you do what you have heard from your father."
"Abraham is our father," they replied. "If you were children of Abraham," said Jesus, "you would do the works of Abraham.
But now you are trying to kill Me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham never did such a thing.
You are doing the works of your father." "We are not illegitimate children," they declared. "Our only Father is God Himself."
Jesus said to them, "If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I have come here from God. I have not come on My own, but He sent Me.
Why do you not understand what I am saying? It is because you are unable to accept My message.

You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!
Which of you can prove Me guilty of sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe Me?
Whoever belongs to God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God."
The Jews answered Him, "Are we not right to say that You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?"
"I do not have a demon," Jesus replied, "but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.
I do not seek My own glory. There is One who seeks it, and He is the Judge.
Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps My word, he will never see death."
"Now we know that You have a demon!" declared the Jews. "Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet You say that anyone who keeps Your word will never taste death.
Are You greater than our father Abraham? He died, as did the prophets. Who do You claim to be?"
Jesus answered, "If I glorify Myself, My glory means nothing. The One who glorifies Me is My Father, of whom you say, 'He is our God.'
You do not know Him, but I know Him. If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know Him, and I keep His word.
Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad."
Then the Jews said to Him, "You are not yet fifty years old, and You have seen Abraham?"
"Truly, truly, I tell you," Jesus declared, "before Abraham was born, I am!"
At this, they picked up stones to throw at Him. But Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area.

context.author: Traditionally the apostle John
context.genre: Theological narrative — a mercy story followed by the most sustained, escalating confrontation in the whole Gospel, climaxing in Jesus' most direct claim to divine identity yet
context.audience: A broad, likely mixed Jewish and Gentile readership toward the end of the first century
context.setting: Still the Feast of Tabernacles, when giant lampstands lit the temple's Court of the Women each night — the vivid, literal backdrop for Jesus' declaration "I am the light of the world," spoken, John notes, right near the temple treasury where those very lamps stood.
context.custom: Roman authorities alone held the legal right of execution in occupied Judea, making the leaders' question about stoning the woman a deliberate trap — any answer risked either contradicting Mosaic law or Roman law. The Law itself required at least two witnesses to establish a capital charge, a detail Jesus later invokes directly regarding His own testimony. Worth knowing: verses 1-11 are a well-known textual question — this passage is absent from the earliest surviving manuscripts of John and shows up in different places in a few later ones, which is why many modern translations set it apart with a note. It's widely regarded as an authentic, very old story about Jesus even so; it simply may not have originally been part of John's own text at this exact spot.
context.timelineImmediate: This chapter moves from a single act of mercy toward an escalating theological confrontation that only intensifies verse by verse, ending with Jesus' most explicit claim yet to eternal, divine identity — a claim His opponents understood so clearly they immediately reached for stones.
context.timelineBible: Jesus' declaration "before Abraham was born, I am" doesn't just claim to predate Abraham chronologically — it uses the exact same absolute "I am" language God uses to name Himself in Exodus 3:14, a claim His hearers understood immediately as nothing less than a claim to be God.
context.sparkNotes: Jesus shows real mercy to a woman facing execution, then declares Himself "the light of the world" and spends the rest of the chapter in an escalating exchange with religious leaders over His identity, His origin, and theirs. The confrontation builds to Jesus' boldest self-claim yet — "before Abraham was born, I am" — language so unmistakably divine that His listeners immediately try to stone Him for blasphemy.

translation.english: I am the light of the world
translation.greek: ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου (egō eimi to phōs tou kosmou)
translation.meaning: The second of Jesus' seven great "I am" declarations in John, spoken against the literal backdrop of the Feast of Tabernacles' nightly temple lighting ceremony.

translation.english: the truth will set you free
translation.greek: ἡ ἀλήθεια ἐλευθερώσει ὑμᾶς (hē alētheia eleutherōsei hymas)
translation.meaning: One of the most quoted lines in the Gospel — Jesus redefines freedom entirely, from political or ancestral status to freedom from slavery to sin itself.

translation.english: before Abraham was born, I am
translation.greek: πρὶν Ἀβραὰμ γενέσθαι ἐγὼ εἰμί (prin Abraam genesthai egō eimi)
translation.meaning: The climactic seventh use of the unqualified "I am" in this chapter alone, deliberately echoing God's own self-naming to Moses in Exodus 3:14 — not merely a claim of existing before Abraham, but of sharing God's own eternal, timeless name.

otBackground.note: The Law's actual penalty for adultery, invoked (and weaponized) by the woman's accusers.
God's own self-naming, "I AM WHO I AM" — directly echoed in Jesus' climactic declaration, "before Abraham was born, I am."
Abraham's faith and his willingness to offer Isaac — background for Jesus' claim that "Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day."

commentary.note: Henry reflects on the woman being caught in the act itself: 'those that promise themselves secrecy in sin deceive themselves... sometimes it proves a mercy to sinners to have their sin brought to light, that they may do no more presumptuously.' Public exposure, however painful, becomes in his reading the occasion for the mercy that follows.

On the accusers' trap, Henry lays out exactly how it was designed to fail either way: if Jesus said release her, He'd appear to override Moses' law; if He said stone her, He'd be reported to Rome for claiming an execution authority only Roman governors held. Jesus' answer, Henry notes, sidesteps the false choice entirely by turning the question back on the accusers themselves.

Guzik points out a detail easy to miss: 'there was also a man involved in this very act of adultery — yet the guilty man was not brought before Jesus for judgment.' The accusers' selective enforcement, he suggests, exposes their real motive as trapping Jesus rather than genuinely upholding the Law.

Lewis does not comment on John 8, but his chapter "The Shocking Alternative" in Mere Christianity is about claims like verse 58, "Before Abraham was born, I am!" He says that a man who claimed to be before Abraham and to be the great I AM would be either a lunatic or a liar, and that nobody should patronize Him as a wise moralist. He asks his reader to face the choice and does not leave a middle option. (Paraphrased; Lewis's works remain under copyright.)

overview.summary: Jesus forgives a woman caught in adultery, then says He is the light of the world. He tells those who believe that the truth will set them free, and says that before Abraham was, I am. They pick up stones, but He slips away.

history.t: Under Rome the Jewish courts could not carry out executions, which sharpens the trap.
Descent from Abraham gave Jews a deep sense of security.

customs.t: Jesus wrote on the ground, and John never says what.
Giant lamps in the Court of Women lit the temple during Tabernacles.

archaeology.t: Broad steps on the temple platform's south side lead to the old Huldah Gates.
Chambers along the Court of Women held the offering chests.

overview.discussion: Jesus told the woman, "Neither do I condemn you; go and sin no more." How do grace and truth fit together?
overview.book: The fourth Gospel · 21 chapters. Written so readers would believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God.
overview.author: John
